content: 1. Sodium bicarbonate and mesalamine interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased urinary pH. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. 2. Omeprazole reduces methamphetamine levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. The time to maximum concentration (Tmax) of amphetamine is reduced when co-administered with omeprazole. Patients should be monitored for changes in clinical effects, and therapy should be adjusted based on clinical response. 3. Omeprazole increases midazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Mitotane decreases omeprazole levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4. When co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates, dosage adjustments may be necessary, and patients should be monitored closely. 5. Omeprazole increases ospemifene levels by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Omeprazole decreases phytoestrogen levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Omeprazole decreases ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Omeprazole increases quazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Ribociclib increases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Omeprazole increases ruxolitinib levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Omeprazole increases ruxolitinib topical levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Sodium bicarbonate and salicylates (non-aspirin) interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased urinary pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Sodium bicarbonate and salsalate interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased urinary pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Sodium bicarbonate decreases strontium ranelate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours when possible. 15. Sodium bicarbonate and sulfasalazine interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased urinary pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Omeprazole increases the toxicity of theophylline through an unspecified mechanism. Prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can cause hypochlorhydria, which may alter gastrointestinal motility, increasing peristalsis in the small intestine and decreasing it in the proximal colon. Patients should be monitored for signs of toxicity. 17. Omeprazole decreases thyroid desiccated levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, and conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 18. Omeprazole increases triazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Omeprazole increases voriconazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Sodium bicarbonate and willow bark interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased urinary pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Omeprazole increases abrocitinib levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. When co-administered with CYP2C19 inhibitors, abrocitinib should be initiated at 50 mg daily. If an adequate response is not achieved after 12 weeks, the dose may be increased to 100 mg daily. 22. Omeprazole decreases acalabrutinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Acalabrutinib solubility decreases with increasing gastric pH. Due to the long-lasting effects of PPIs, separating doses may not eliminate the interaction. Alternative drugs should be considered. 23. Sodium bicarbonate decreases acebutolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 24. Acetazolamide increases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Patients should be monitored closely. 25. Sodium bicarbonate decreases alendronate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 26. Sodium bicarbonate decreases allopurinol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 27. Omeprazole increases alprazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Patients should be monitored closely. 28. Sodium bicarbonate increases amantadine levels or effects due to changes in urinary pH toward alkalinity, which may lead to drug accumulation and increased adverse reactions. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored for adverse reactions. 29. Omeprazole increases ambrisentan levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Patients should be monitored closely. 30. Amobarbital decreases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Patients should be monitored closely. 31. Sodium bicarbonate increases amphetamine levels or effects through passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Omeprazole reduces gastric acidity, which decreases the time to Tmax for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine. The area under the curve (AUC) remains unaffected. Patients should be monitored closely. 32. Omeprazole decreases ampicillin levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Sodium bicarbonate also decreases ampicillin levels by increasing gastric pH. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 33. Anastrozole increases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Apalutamide decreases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Apalutamide is a strong CYP2C19 inducer, and co-administration with CYP2C19 substrates can result in lower drug exposure. Alternative drugs should be considered, and patients should be monitored for loss of therapeutic effect. 35. Armodafinil increases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Patients should be monitored closely. 36. Sodium bicarbonate and aspirin interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased urinary pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 37. Sodium bicarbonate decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. PPIs should not exceed a dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken approximately 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 38. Sodium bicarbonate decreases atenolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 39. Omeprazole increases avapritinib levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should be monitored closely. 40. Omeprazole increases axitinib levels by affecting hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should be monitored closely. 41. Sodium bicarbonate decreases azithromycin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 42. Sodium bicarbonate and balsalazide interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased urinary pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. Sodium bicarbonate increases bearberry levels or effects through passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Patients should be monitored closely. 44. Omeprazole decreases belumosudil levels by increasing gastric pH. When co-administered with PPIs, the belumosudil dosage should be increased to 200 mg twice daily. Patients should be monitored closely. 45. Omeprazole increases belzutifan levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Belzutifan is a CYP2C19 substrate, and co-administration with CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase the incidence or severity of adverse effects. Patients should be monitored for anemia and hypoxia, and the belzutifan dose should be reduced as recommended. 46. Sodium bicarbonate decreases benazepril effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Patients should be monitored closely. 47. Sodium bicarbonate increases benzphetamine levels or effects through passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Patients should be monitored closely. 48. Sodium bicarbonate decreases betaxolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 49. Omeprazole increases bismuth subsalicylate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Sodium bicarbonate decreases bisoprolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of these agents by 2 hours. Patients should be monitored closely. 51. Blessed thistle decreases omeprazole effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Blessed thistle also decreases sodium bicarbonate effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is theoretical, and patients should be monitored closely. 52. Bortezomib increases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Patients should be monitored closely. 53. Bosentan decreases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
